survey: The object is a spiral topiary bush in a round planter made of stone blocks. It stands on a terracotta paved path, with a lawn and a trimmed hedge behind it. The camera is a little above the object and looks slightly down. The planter rim is an even, fairly open ellipse, and the soil inside it is visible, which fits that downward view. The blocks on the front of the ring are wide and face the camera; the blocks toward the sides get narrower and turn away, following the curve of the ring. The bottom edge of the planter is an ellipse that matches the rim, and it sits flat on the paving. The paving stones and the curving path edge lie flat on the same ground plane. The bush rises from the soil in four stacked tiers that get smaller toward the top. The top of each tier shows as a ledge seen slightly from above, and the edges of those ledges curve down at the sides. That agrees with the planter's ellipse. The leaves overlap and turn as they wrap around each round tier. The top tuft is also seen slightly from above. The bush's central axis is a straight vertical line. The hedge and lawn behind it are level and below a horizon that fits the same raised camera.
